Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The main problem is that the camera sometimes fails to power on after it has been in my bag for several hours. When it does turn on, the top display comes on, but the rear screen can stay black. The problem is intermittent rather than constant. I tested it at home with each of my 2 batteries, and it happened with both, although not every time. One battery is the original Aster battery and the other is a replacement from the same maker. I have not tested the camera with another charger, so I don’t know whether charging is part of the problem.

There is also a separate issue with the control dial on the back. It turns, but some changes to the menu selection do not register unless I turn it slowly and try again. The shutter button still takes a picture when the camera is on. I have not noticed a crack in the body or damage to the lens mount. I told the intake person that I did not want those details treated as proof of a particular fault; they are just what I have observed. The technician said, “We’ll check the power issue and the dial before we put a repair amount on paper.” Please include the technician’s inspection results in the estimate, even if the results are inconclusive.

For context, the camera was in my carry-on during a rainy weekend in March, but it stayed inside a closed bag and I did not see water on it. I’m mentioning that because the intake form asks about moisture, not because I know that moisture caused anything. The camera has not been dropped, to my knowledge. The last time I cleaned it was in April, using a dry cloth on the outside only. I have not opened the body or tried to repair it myself. Please avoid stating that there is water damage or impact damage unless the inspection actually supports that finding.

I also want the estimate to make it clear which charges are for work already performed and which are only possible future charges. I understand that the shop may need to inspect the camera to identify the fault, but I do not know whether the initial inspection fee is already included in the estimate I received at intake. Please list that fee separately and say whether it is charged even if I decline a repair. The intake person gave me a printed receipt but did not give me a repair price or a completion date, so I am not asking you to confirm either one from that conversation.

Please organize the estimate around these items, with the description and amount for each one where it can be determined:
1. The inspection and diagnosis of the intermittent power problem, including whether the camera behaves differently with either battery.
2. The inspection of the rear control dial and any cleaning or adjustment that may be proposed for it.
3. Any parts that might be needed, listed separately from labor, with the part name and whether it is new or refurbished if that information is available.
4. Labor for each proposed repair, rather than one unexplained combined amount.
5. Any additional fee, including the initial inspection fee, and whether it applies if I decide not to proceed.

Please use the file named below when checking the accessory notes I sent with the camera. It lists the winter items I packed with it, and I don’t want the filename changed because I use it to identify that attachment:
winter-kit-list.txt

The accessory notes mention a padded camera wrap, two spare memory cards, and a small cleaning brush. Those items were in the same bag, but I kept them separate from the camera when I handed it over. I’m not asking the shop to value or inspect the accessories. I only want the file referred to accurately if the estimate needs to mention what was supplied or what was not supplied. The camera’s shoulder strap and body cap were attached when I left it at the counter, and the two batteries were in the side pocket of the camera bag. Please let me know if the estimate is based on the camera alone or also includes handling of those items.

One condition matters before any repair is started: if the total proposed repair amount is more than $350, please contact me with the estimate and wait for my approval. If the amount is $350 or less, please still send the estimate and do not treat the amount as permission to begin work. If the inspection reveals more than one possible cause, please list the alternatives and the cost associated with each, rather than combining them into a single assumed repair. If a part is unavailable, say so in the estimate instead of substituting a different part without asking me.

I would appreciate wording that separates what the technician observed from what remains uncertain. For example, a note that the camera failed to power on during a test would be different from a conclusion about why it failed. If the fault does not appear during inspection, please say that it was not reproduced rather than suggesting it has been fixed. The same applies to the dial: please distinguish a recorded test result from a possible cleaning or replacement.
